mission.title: coredns: 1.14.6: intermittent NOERROR/empty-A for external names with autopath + cache (prefetch/serve_stale) on parallel A/AAAA lookups
mission.description: 1.14.6: intermittent NOERROR/empty-A for external names with autopath + cache (prefetch/serve_stale) on parallel A/AAAA lookups. This issue affects 6+ users.

steps.title: Identify coredns troubleshoot symptoms
steps.description:
Check for the issue in your coredns deployment:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n coredns -l app.kubernetes.io/name=coredns
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=coredns -n coredns --tail=100 | grep -i error
```
Look for errors or warnings in the logs that may indicate the issue.

steps.title: Review coredns configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant coredns configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n coredns -l app.kubernetes.io/name=coredns
kubectl get configmap -n coredns -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=coredns
```
### What happened

After upgrading CoreDNS **1.13.1 → 1.14.6** (helm chart 1.46.2 → 1.47.0, **Corefile unchanged — byte-identical**), clients across the cluster began intermittently receiving **NOERROR responses with an empty A answer section** for

steps.title: Apply the fix for 1.14.6: intermittent NOERROR/empty-A for external names…
Upgrade coredns to include the fix
steps.description:
If the fix is included in a newer release, upgrade coredns:
```bash
helm repo update
helm upgrade coredns coredns/coredns --namespace coredns
```
Verify the upgrade:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n coredns
helm list -n coredns
```

steps.title: Confirm 1.14.6: intermittent NOERROR/empty-A for external… is resolved
steps.description:
Verify the fix by checking that the original error no longer occurs:
```bash
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=coredns -n coredns --tail=50 --since=5m
kubectl get events -n coredns --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm that the issue symptoms are gone.

resolution.summary: I now have a reproducer using the actual Kubernetes plugin with `pods verified`, its client-go informers and Pod index, backed by a local list/watch API fixture. My earlier harness used a static search path and missed the dependency on the client's IP.
